description:
FILED s452aa (Opus agent AA, measured while closing #738).  PRE-EXISTING and
unrelated to that fix.

    $ cat ex7.pl
    print "x\n";
    exit 7;

    $ perl ex7.pl   ; echo rc=$?      ->  rc=7
    $ ./runpcl ex7.pl ; echo rc=$?    ->  rc=0

The EMITTED program is right: run the same file's CL through SBCL directly
(`sbcl --control-stack-size 512 --load cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --load prog.lisp`)
and the process exits 7.  The loss is in `runpcl`, which does not propagate its
child's status.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: no measurement runner reads runpcl's
status (the sweep and the companion spawn SBCL themselves and read TAP), so
this has never falsified a count.  It DOES falsify any hand probe of the form
`./runpcl p.pl; echo $?`, and that is how it was found -- the #738 END-block
exit-code check read 0 from runpcl and 7 from SBCL for the same program.

BAR: `./runpcl` exits with the program's status for a top-level `exit N`, for
an `exit N` inside an END block (perl: the LAST such status wins, task #738),
and for a die (perl: 255-ish; measure rather than assume).  `./runt` and `./clt`
are the siblings to check in the same pass.
subject: `./runpcl` always exits 0 -- the program status is not propagated (the emitted CL is right)
